 Mobile Pixel Weather now lets you report inaccurate weather conditions
 A new card at the bottom of the weather details page features a new user feedback option. Chethan Rao AssembleDebug • Nov 13, 2026 — 5:56 AM ET 
 • • Rita El Khoury / Android Authority Add Android Authority on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover TL;DR 
 The latest version of the Pixel Weather app lets you report inaccurate weather conditions.
 Users get to choose from a range of weather conditions and temperature options before submitting their report.
 This user feedback option comes amid a wave of online complaints about Pixel Weather.
 Google’s Pixel Weather could soon let users report inaccurate weather forecasts directly from the app. In the past, we’ve seen incidents where Pixel Weather’s data has been off the mark , and it now looks like Google is taking steps to fix that.

 This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

 Version 1.1.20261012 of the Pixel Weather app includes a dedicated card named Report current weather at the bottom of your current location’s weather details page. “Share the current weather condition to improve local forecasts,” the accompanying description reads.
 Tapping the Submit a report button opens a bottom sheet containing sections named Current temperature and Current conditions. In the temperature section, you can choose from Warmer, Colder, or Seems accurate.
 By contrast, the Current conditions section covers a broad range of options, including Cloudy, Clear, Rain showers, Sleet or hail, Snow showers, Strong thunderstorms, and Low visibility.
 This bottom sheet interface also shows the current conditions and temperature, so users know exactly what inaccuracy they’re reporting. Google says it will collect the feedback, device location, along with “some diagnostic information” to improve future forecasts, adding that this data won’t be associated with the user’s Google account.
 This user feedback feature didn’t appear out of nowhere. Users have long complained  about Pixel Weather’s inaccuracies , and Google seems to have decided it needs to do more.
 We’re seeing the new user reporting options across a couple of Pixel devices we have on hand. You can try it yourself by sideloading the latest Pixel Weather bundle from APKMirror .
 We still don’t know exactly how Google will act on these submissions or whether they’ll affect future weather forecasts in any meaningful way. Still, this is a step in the right direction and will give Pixel owners a way to accurately describe what’s wrong with the weather reading.
